proposed_from.topic: K1 prove the transported-mean minimax LOWER root-risk phase diagram m^-1/2 plus n^-1/2 for a<1, sqrt(log n/n) at a=1, and n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)} for a>1 when f_S~x^a and f_T stays positive at zero, together with the matching deterministic truncated-oracle bias-standard-deviation envelope. K2 construct an executable capped calibrated-OT plus boundary local-polynomial realized-design linear/Hoeffding certificate, without claiming a data-measurable minimax upper bound or frontier attainment. K3 give a finite-sample fixed-class observable-radius coverage certificate, without claiming frontier-order expected length. K4 prove the matching lower bounds and the explicit nonadaptation obstruction; leave executable self-similar adaptation open. Include the boundary-bump and critical multiscale witnesses and the RICOT cardiomyopathy consumer. The measurable same-class upper bound, stochastic held-out weight localization, and frontier-order interval length remain open research objects.

seed_details.one_line: Sharp two-sample polynomial-boundary minimax frontier with a multiscale critical lower bound.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Sections 3--4, Theorem 1, Theorem 4, the exact remainder proof, and the Discussion were read from the arXiv source; bounded density-ratio overlap is the first boundary crossed by this seed.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global finite-variance influence-function step by the truncated representer norm and a boundary modulus; at \(a=1\), replace a two-point test by a multiscale mixture.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact pair of transported mean, polynomial boundary density, and rate \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) found no occupied theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is uniform over a factorized Hölder class and includes an explicit estimator and a matching converse, not a single engineered law.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Khan and Tamer because polynomial inverse-weight tails already determine irregular rates.
seed_details.rebuttal: Khan and Tamer do not compute this linear-functional modulus, the critical logarithm, the smoothness-dependent exponent, or the independent target-sample floor.

seed_details.one_line: Semiparametric efficiency-breakdown frontier for unbounded transport Riesz weights.
seed_details.anchor_read: The efficient-influence-function theorem and its pathwise-derivative proof identify \(r=f_T/f_S\); the standing overlap assumption bounds \(r\), and the Discussion does not derive a polynomial weak-overlap efficiency frontier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Recompute the tangent-functional norm when \(r\notin L^\infty(P_S)\), then identify the exact point at which the canonical gradient leaves \(L^2(P_S)\).
seed_details.destination_search: RICOT and transported-effect efficiency searches found regular bounds but no local asymptotic minimax experiment at the \(a=1\) boundary.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This lane isolates an efficiency object rather than relabeling the minimax rate theorem, but it is narrower than the full frontier.
seed_details.referee_objection: The efficiency bound is infinite exactly when the representer is not square-integrable, so the result is definitional.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection lands for \(a\ge1\); the nontrivial content would be the replacement local experiment and normalization, so the seed is not selected alone.

seed_details.one_line: Critical Gaussian limit for a boundary-spliced transported-mean estimator at \(a=1\).
seed_details.anchor_read: The published abstract and accepted-manuscript theorem summary were checked: untrimmed extreme-weight estimators can have stable limits and require modified resampling, while no smooth boundary extrapolation or transported target process is treated.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the stable-tail normalization by a triangular-array central limit theorem for truncated calibrated residuals plus the correlated boundary local-polynomial term.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for critical logarithmic transported-mean normality under \(f_S(x)\asymp x\) returned trimming and heavy-tail papers but no such limit theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law is the headline and must be derived from primitive weight and leverage bounds rather than assumed.
seed_details.referee_objection: A Lindeberg theorem after truncation makes the Gaussian limit routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The boundary fit, learned calibration weights, target empirical average, and nonnegligible bias share the chosen scale, so joint linearization is not a scalar truncated-sum CLT.

seed_details.one_line: Transported policy-learning regret under polynomial source depletion and a target margin condition.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, lower-bound theorem and fuzzy-hypothesis proof, two-stage calibration theorem, and Conclusion were read from source; the paper treats scalar moments, not target-population policy regret.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After constructing a boundary-local CATE score, convert score error to welfare regret through a target margin inequality and rebuild the lower alternatives around policy sign changes.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found transported off-policy learning and efficient policy-value estimation under covariate shift, but not a polynomial-boundary regret exponent with a matching causal lower bound.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a genuine decision target, but it adds a margin parameter and moves away from the scalar cardiomyopathy estimand fixed by the brief.
seed_details.referee_objection: The result is an immediate plug-in of weak-overlap CATE rates into a standard Tsybakov margin inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: A converse would require policies whose sign changes occur on the depleted boundary while preserving the target margin; nevertheless the scalar frontier should be solved first.

seed_details.one_line: Riesz-calibrated optimal transport spliced to boundary local-polynomial extrapolation.
seed_details.anchor_read: The empirical calibrated program, multiplicative-tilt proposition, calibration-rate proof, exact stochastic decomposition, central-limit theorem, and Discussion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global weighted Gram-matrix and bounded-tilt argument by an interior \([h,1]\) calibration inequality and add an explicit boundary local-polynomial remainder.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact target--method search for Riesz-calibrated optimal transport plus boundary local polynomial found RICOT and separate overlap-extrapolation papers, but no combined risk theorem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The estimator is paired with the exact frontier and not offered as an unbenchmarked algorithm.
seed_details.referee_objection: Exact spline calibration makes the optimal-transport offset asymptotically irrelevant, so this is just series regression in decorative OT notation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The theorem must quantify the admissible transport offset and calibration residual under diverging boundary weights; it also yields a procedure continuous with the published RICOT implementation.

seed_details.one_line: Fixed-Hölder-class bias-aware honest intervals across the three overlap regimes.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, general fixed-length interval theorems, local-polynomial maximum-bias theorem and proof, comparison section, and conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the regular fixed-design equivalent-kernel variance by the joint variance of interior calibrated residuals, boundary extrapolation, and an independent target empirical average.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found honest local-polynomial intervals and weak-overlap stable-law inference separately, but no fixed-class transported interval at the \(a=1\) logarithmic boundary.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The interval is tied to an explicit estimator, bias envelope, and uniform coverage theorem.
seed_details.referee_objection: Folded-normal critical values transfer immediately once a bias bound and standard error are written down.
seed_details.rebuttal: The new theorem is the uniform normal approximation and valid joint bias envelope for learned calibration weights at a diverging critical variance.

seed_details.one_line: Bandwidth-snooping correction for data-searched transport truncation scales.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, overlap-trimming application, main Gaussian-process theorem, Appendix equivalence result, and Conclusion were opened on the publisher page; the paper explicitly leaves shrinking weak-overlap cutoffs for future work.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed-bandwidth-ratio Brownian approximation by a nonstationary process whose variance changes from finite to logarithmic to polynomial across the searched range.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located gives a snooping correction when the bandwidth search itself crosses the square-integrability boundary of a transported Riesz weight.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The critical process is named, but this is an inference extension rather than the primary frontier.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a direct application of the published bandwidth-snooping critical value.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their weak-overlap discussion fixes the trimming range and expressly does not cover shrinking cutoffs with an infinite variance bound.

seed_details.one_line: Honest adaptation to unknown \((a,s)\) under explicit boundary self-similarity.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, between-class modulus lower bound, ordered-modulus construction, examples, and concluding discussion were checked through the arXiv and journal versions; the theory is abstract and does not compute the transported weighted-design modulus.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute the between-class modulus in the \(L^2(x^a dx)\) observation norm, then use persistent dyadic boundary approximation error to make the active bias scale observable.
seed_details.destination_search: Bull covers self-similar bands and Armstrong--Kolesár cover fixed-class scalar intervals, but the target--method pair of transported weak-overlap linear functional and boundary self-similarity was unoccupied.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The restriction is explicit and realistic for functions with a persistent leading boundary term; unrestricted adaptation is separately ruled out.
seed_details.referee_objection: Bull already proves self-similarity necessary and sufficient for honest adaptation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Bull's object is a function band under a regular observation norm, not a two-sample scalar functional whose norm changes at \(a=1\).

seed_details.one_line: Population characterization and correction of raw entropic-transport boundary bias.
seed_details.anchor_read: The kernel fixed-point proposition, regularization-bias expansion and proof, calibration KKT representation, and noncanonical-weight proposition were read from source.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Redo the heat-kernel expansion on a support boundary where \(f_S(x)\asymp x^a\), retaining boundary flux terms that are absent from the interior compact-set expansion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found entropic boundary-bias analyses for transport maps, but no causal Riesz-weight decomposition at a vanishing source density.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a correction regime, but it does not by itself establish the statistical frontier.
seed_details.referee_objection: The boundary term is a routine correction to the paper's interior heat expansion.
seed_details.rebuttal: The singular ratio invalidates the uniform expansion and changes the estimability class, but the result is best retained as an estimator lemma inside the frontier project.

proposed_from.literature_map: 1. Burman, Gamalo, Ghosal, and Kundu (2026) identify the target-to-trial density ratio as the Riesz representer, prove calibrated-OT weight convergence, and obtain regular efficient inference under bounded overlap; their global weighted-Gram and influence-function arguments are the exact proof boundary. 2. Khan and Tamer (2010) show that arbitrarily large inverse weights create irregular identification with tail-dependent rates, but do not specialize the modulus to a two-sample transported Hölder mean. 3. Zhang, Liu, Wang, and Teng (2025) provide a generic covariate-shift moment lower bound and two-stage calibration upper bound, yet work with a bounded likelihood ratio and retain logarithmic slack. 4. Donoho (1994) supplies the modulus-of-continuity lower bound and near-minimax affine recovery construction adapted here to the weighted boundary norm. 5. Ma and Wang (2020) derive tail-dependent Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits and use boundary local polynomials to estimate trimming bias; their scalar tail argument must be rebuilt for calibrated transport plus target sampling. 6. Heiler and Kazak (2021) confirm that ordinary bootstrap inference can fail under extreme inverse weights, motivating a primitive critical normal approximation rather than assumed Gaussianity. 7. Orihara, Komukai, and Li (2026) retain the ATE through polynomial extrapolation of overlap-weighted estimands, but assume an estimand-path approximation instead of deriving a fixed-Hölder boundary remainder. 8. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) provide the fixed-class folded-normal interval and exact worst-case local-polynomial bias logic used for honest inference. 9. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) provide the bandwidth-search Gaussian-process correction and explicitly leave shrinking weak-overlap cutoffs outside their theorem. 10. Cai and Low (2004) characterize adaptive interval length through between-class moduli; Bull (2012) supplies a self-similarity mechanism for adaptive bands. 11. The exact polynomial-boundary transported rate, the RICOT--local-polynomial splice, and the critical \(a=1\) honest interval were not occupied in the searched literature. 12. The writing exemplar used is Burman et al. (2026); the method exemplars used are Donoho (1994), Ma and Wang (2020), Armstrong and Kolesár (2020), and Cai and Low (2004).

banked_reason: The note proves no matching upper bound for any data-measurable estimator, so the contribution remains below the field floor.
